surface_forms: celui qu’il appelait un simple « joueur de flûte »

appraisal_events.evidence: « Oh ! mon Dieu, comme tu souffres », s’écria-t-elle, les traits bouleversés ; elle sort de nuit acheter le cognac qu’elle désapprouve, revient « un peu rouge », l’air gêné, « une expression de lassitude et de découragement », et le narrateur sent « sur ses joues fraîches quelque chose de mouillé ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The retrospective narration plainly elevates the grandmother by staging her self-overriding devotion — she procures the alcohol she disapproves of and hides her tears — and by letting the reader see the sacrifice the young narrator does not.

appraisal_events.evidence: « mon corps avait voulu obtenir exactement ce qu’il méritait de pitié » ; « Feignait-elle de n’y prêter aucune attention, il me demandait d’insister. Parfois j’allais trop loin » ; et enfin « Je trouvai que c’était montrer bien de l’indifférence pour moi, et je me retins pour ne pas la lui reprocher ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrating voice indicts its younger self: he extorts his grandmother's pity as a physiological due, misses her tears, and converts her one absence into a grievance about her indifference — an egotism the passage exposes rather than excuses.

status_effects.explanation: She comes out clearly elevated: her love is shown as costly, concealed, and unrewarded, and the narration endorses it without irony.
The same scene shows her losing ground emotionally — no longer 'maître de ses émotions qu’autrefois', red-faced, discouraged, weeping and leaving abruptly.
He is locally lowered by the narration's exposure of his exacted pity and his unjust reproach of indifference.
Within the dyad he nevertheless gains leverage: his grandmother yields to his signalled suffering, insisting until she gives in and goes out for the cognac.

ambiguities: The opening self-reproach — « il me sembla que je méritais vraiment le dédain de M. de Norpois » for being exalted by « une odeur de moisi » rather than by an important idea — is voiced as blame but framed by the unexplained « une telle félicité » and by the deferral « je remis à plus tard de chercher pourquoi », so it is unclear whether the passage ratifies Norpois's contempt or ironizes it; read as ironized, it would not diminish the narrator at all, which is why it is not made a separate event.

The closing beat is formally undecidable at the level of the young narrator: « quelque chose de mouillé dont je ne sus pas si c’était l’humidité de l’air nocturne » and the grandmother's unexplained daytime absence could be read as her withdrawal (a diminishment of her), but the accumulated signs — her flushed face, embarrassment, discouragement and abrupt exit — make the tears reading dominant, so the diminishment is assigned to the narrator's misreading instead.
